disputed_claims: L12's framing that PID 1146711 is an 'unaccounted orphan ... invisible to systemd/journalctl' and 'not present anywhere in the current ps -ef output' is disproved by system_watch.log: three separate ps-aux snapshots taken DURING the incident window (07:51, 07:54, 07:57) all show PID 1146711 alive as 'python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0', started 07:48, running continuously ~10min. L12 evidently ran its own ps -ef check AFTER the process had already exited (some minutes after 07:59:17) and mistook 'not running at query time' for 'never existed / unidentifiable'.

The 'invisible to journalctl' framing is also overstated: journalctl (system, not filtered to hermes-gateway/dashboard units) shows the surrounding process tree being created at the same moment -- app-gnome-hermes-1146550.scope started by gnome-shell at 07:48:23, hermes.desktop[1146565/1146566] Electron startup lines at 07:48:24-27, and app-org.chromium.Chromium-1146566.scope -- consistent with PID 1146711 being the Hermes Desktop app's embedded local backend server, spawned by the Electron main process (not by systemd, hence absent from `journalctl -u hermes-gateway.service`/`hermes-dashboard.service`, but present in the general journal and in ps).

The consolidated.md minority note 'L12's orphan PID 1146711 -- never identified... could be a leaked/zombie previous gateway process, a stray hermes CLI, or something else entirely' is too pessimistic given available evidence; the cmdline in system_watch.log ('hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0') is a specific, known Hermes entry point (the desktop app's local API/backend server), not a generic stray CLI invocation or zombie gateway.
confirmed_claims: PID 1146711 is NOT running right now: `ps -p 1146711` returns no matching process.

There is no dmesg/journalctl (--user or system) log line naming PID 1146711 as a subject except one incidental im-config child-process log at 07:58:05 ('PPID=1146711'), and no systemd Stopping/Started cycle for hermes-gateway.service/hermes-dashboard.service at 07:59 -- confirming it was not managed by either tracked systemd unit, consistent with L12's core observation that it doesn't match the gateway/dashboard MainPIDs.
The errors.log/agent.log lines confirming the 07:59:17 halt-trigger retired-WAL capture for PID 1146711 are real and match L12's citation exactly.

cron.scheduler subprocesses spawned via systemd-run scopes ARE visible in journalctl during the window (07:48:07, 07:51:08, 07:54:08, 07:57:09, 07:59:09) -- these are a separate, already-identified class of short-lived transient writer distinct from 1146711, so 1146711 is not one of the cron worker scopes.

system_watch.log (a periodic ps-aux snapshot logger not searched by L12) DOES contain PID 1146711, with full cmdline '/home/ian-koratsky/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0', STIME 07:48, alongside a concurrently-started Electron process (PID 1146695, 'Hermes --type=zygote --no-sandbox') under the same apps/desktop/release tree -- this identifies 1146711 as the Hermes Desktop app's locally-spawned backend server process (the `hermes serve` command the desktop app shells out to on launch), not a rogue or unidentifiable process.

This does NOT overturn the swarm's core multi-writer theory -- it actually strengthens it: PID 1146711 is a genuine, legitimate, but registry-bypassing THIRD writer process (a manually-launched desktop app instance opening its own SessionDB against the same default state.db) distinct from gateway/dashboard/cron, exactly the class of 'ad-hoc invocation' contributing factor already named in consolidated.md's root-cause list.
missing_gap: None of the 5 lanes appear to have grepped ~/.hermes/logs/system_watch.log, which is the one artifact that actually resolves PID 1146711's identity (via periodic ps-aux snapshots). This should be folded back into the consolidated theory: replace 'orphan PID, never identified' with 'identified as a `hermes_cli.main serve` process spawned by a manually-launched Hermes Desktop app instance around 07:48, a legitimate but registry-bypassing third writer against the default state.db -- consistent with, not contradictory to, the existing ad-hoc-CLI-writer explanation.'
verdict: Theory holds and is now stronger: PID 1146711 is fully identifiable (Hermes Desktop app's local `hermes_cli.main serve` backend, started ~07:48 alongside the Electron desktop process, exited by 07:59:17 halt), not a mysterious rogue/orphan. L12's 'unaccounted orphan' framing was based on an incomplete evidence sweep (post-hoc ps -ef and a narrow journalctl/errors.log grep) that missed system_watch.log's contemporaneous ps snapshots proving the process was alive, named, and traceable to the desktop app launch. This closes the swarm's single most 'unexplained' data point as a known process, and slots cleanly into the existing multi-writer root-cause theory as another instance of the already-cited 'ad-hoc manual CLI invocation, bypasses the registry' contributing factor -- no new causal mechanism is needed.
